subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the vehicle structure for the TypeScript module, deciding it doesn't need a full joint skeleton like a creature would—just a simple static setup with wheels, keeping the rig minimal since it's scenery rather than an animated character.

Now I'm designing an armored 6x6 truck: roughly 9m long, 3m wide, 3.2m tall, facing +Z, with three wheel axles and specific box dimensions for the chassis. I'm also sketching out which paint kits and SVG textures to import (hazard stripes, headlights, HUD screens, license plates) and laying out coordinates for the chassis frame and six wheels using cylinder geometry.

Still placing wheel assemblies...

Now I'm sketching the cab shape as an extruded profile in the side plane, defining its outline from rear to hood with a sloped windshield leading into the roofline.

For the windshield I'm computing its dimensions and orientation from the slope geometry, positioning it with a normal vector pointing forward-up, lifting it slightly off the surface, and insetting it narrower than the cab width.

I'll add a textured plane with a windshield-reflection SVG layered over a dark glass base, then similar side window planes mirrored on the left and right at a set height range, each with their own svg texture. Next I'm planning hood details like vents and sloped panel lines.

Now I'm sketching the front-end armor: a sloped grille plane with a neon texture, a dark metal bumper box with a hazard-stripe front texture, and a wedge-shaped ram blade extruded from a trapezoid outline.

For details I'm adding glowing headlight boxes near the grille in cyan/white, plus a magenta roof light bar positioned above the windshield area.

For the roof, I'm planning a sensor dome, satellite dish, and antenna array, and deciding whether to add a small remote weapon station on the cab roof alongside a larger railgun turret on the rear cargo bed. The cargo area itself I'm shaping into an armored container box sized to fit behind the cab.

Now I'm fleshing out the container's details: vertical rib panels, decal planes for emblems and neon text, a rear door with hazard stripes and handles, and a rooftop missile pod with clustered tubes. I'm also sketching in fuel tank cylinders and twin exhaust stacks mounted behind the cab.

Adding glowing exhaust tips, cyan underglow strips along the chassis, mirrors with support arms, door handles, step rails, mud flaps, a tow hook, cables, antenna whips, and a glowing "NOMAD-77" neon sign textured onto a dark backing panel for the container. I'm also planning rear tail lights that glow red, a bumper, and maybe a solar or radar panel instead of a drone pad. For the color scheme I'm settling on gunmetal, near-black, and magenta accent tones.

Now I'm refining the palette further, landing on a dark teal-gray body with tan panels and a camo-mottled texture over gunmetal for the container, giving it a militarized cyberpunk look. I'm listing out the textures I need—windshield, side window, grille, hazard lights, neon sign, emblem, hood vents, stencil numbers, and warning labels—around eight total. Then I'm setting up helper functions for building boxes and cylinders, plus a mirrored loop for symmetric parts like the side mirrors.

I'm working out how plane geometry textures get mapped with glow/emissive effects, making sure the material and texture logic plays nicely together, and checking the directional math so a side-view decal plane faces outward correctly when mirrored for the opposite side.

Now I'm setting up the gun barrel orientation and sketching the turret geometry with a lathed base and housing box.

I'm placing the railgun assembly on top of the container, positioning the base, housing, and twin rail barrels with glowing coil rings, working out how they extend forward relative to the cab roof and container top.

I need to resolve clearance conflicts between the barrel's forward reach and the RWS turret and light bar, so I'm shortening the barrel length and repositioning the turret further back to avoid overlap.

Now I'm adding missile pods to the container sides with protruding dark cylinders to suggest tube openings, plus a decal texture for the circular pod grid pattern. I'll also add small hub nut details to the wheels to finish off the surface detailing.

Working out wheel geometry now, deciding on tire, rim, neon ring, and lug nut placement with each wheel positioned relative to the chassis and container width so everything clears properly.

I notice the tire overlaps with the container at the current heights, so I'm adjusting the container's y range upward to avoid interpenetration, while making sure fender boxes still sit correctly beside the cab and above the tire.

I'm checking wheel placement against the cab so the front tire doesn't collide with the cab body—adjusting the wheel x-position and track width so the tire sits just outside the cab's half-width, with only a slight acceptable overlap into the container.

Now I'm sizing the fender flares, positioning the wheels vertically so they rest flush on the floor, and setting the chassis frame box dimensions and position, plus placing bumpers at the front and rear.

Positioning rear axles and wheels along the z-axis with spacing so tires don't overlap, then adding side skirts and fuel tank cylinders near the wheel wells.

Now I'm adding neon underglow strips beneath the chassis, then moving on to cab details like a roof light bar, sensor dome, antennas with a blinking red light, and a wedge-shaped roof fairing deflector connecting the cab to the container.

I'm adding side armor plates and door seam details with thin dark boxes for seams, handles, and steps, then working out the cab's side window shape — figuring out where the roof slope intersects the window region so the parallelogram outline matches the sloped roofline correctly.

Still shaping windshield polygon...

For the windshield I'll keep it simple dark glass with a cyan gradient reflection, no center pillar needed. Then I'm adding side mirrors as small rods extending from the cab with a flat mirror box attached at the end.

Now I'm positioning the front grille, placing a tilted plane facing forward near the sloped front edge, then adding hood vents as a slightly raised plane on the hood's angled surface.

For headlights I'm computing glowing box positions on either side of the front face, sizing them so they embed just within the grille depth without poking through.

Now I'm sketching the bumper geometry and checking for overlap with the plow blade, deciding to make the plow a thin wedge tapering from a wider base to a narrow top so it leans forward without clipping into the ground, then positioning a hazard-stripe texture plane flush against the bumper's front face.

Since that caused a conflict, I'm scrapping the separate plow idea and instead designing the bumper as an angled push bar with a hazard stripe plane and a row of small spike cones running along the bottom edge, plus adding a winch cylinder tucked into the bumper. For the rear, I'm placing a mirrored bumper box with glowing red tail-light boxes on the container's back face.

For the rear door I'm layering a hazard-striped texture with a lock bar detail on the lower band, then adding container side ribs as a series of thin vertical boxes spaced along the sides with horizontal cross rails, plus a neon sign decal plane -- though I need to double check it doesn't overlap the rib positions.

Rethinking placement: ribs cluster near both ends (z around 0.7, 0.3, -3.6, -3.95) leaving a clear central span for the sign at z=-1.95, and I'm texturing the sign with "2077" and "MIL-SEC" Latin text with cyan neon glow on one side, plus a hexagonal emblem on the other.

I'm giving the glow texture a dark backing rect so non-glow regions read as unlit, then adding roof details -- panel boxes, vents, and a satellite dish made from a partial sphere cap for the container's top.

Since a sphere cap would show culled back faces when viewed as a concave bowl, I'm switching to a lathe profile instead, defining the rim and inner wall points carefully to avoid self-intersection.

Positioning the dish on the cab roof with a tilt, then moving on to simple rod-based whip antennas and skipping the AESA panel and dash details for now.

I'm also planning a dome-and-glow sensor for the cab roof plus corner camera pods, and working out exhaust stack placement on the outside of the cab sides so they clear the container's front edge.

For the remote weapon station I'm adding a base cylinder, mounting box, gun barrel, and glow sensor, then scattering small reactive-armor tiles in a grid along the lower cab sides.

I'm continuing that armor theme onto the container's lower side panels with rows of tiles, then moving up to design the roof details — deck plates, turret ring base, ammo boxes, cable conduit, missile pods, and antennas — before heading underneath to add differential pods, a driveshaft cylinder, and the chassis frame box tying it all together.

Now I'm positioning axles and differential spheres along the frame, then adding shock absorber rods connecting the chassis to each axle near the wheels, aiming to push the total part count toward 250. I'm also setting up the hull paint using a panelled iron texture with slight tarnish, rivets, and a defined aspect ratio for the metal look.

Checking texel density for the paint sheet, I realize the default resolution leaves rivets under one texel, so I'm bumping the paint texture up to 2048 to keep seams and small details sharp, while limiting full painting to larger panels and using flat colors elsewhere to control cost.

Defining a color palette, I'm setting dusty gunmetal and tan camo mottle paints for hull and container surfaces, flat tones for armor tiles, and a set of accent constants for steel, tan, cyan, magenta, amber, red, glass, tire, and rim hues.

I'm wrapping flat-colored parts with a glow effect for emissive highlights, and importing the glow and clockwork kits for metal and panel textures. Now I'm drafting the SVG sources for the windshield and side window, giving the windshield a dark teal base with semi-transparent cyan reflections, a dark frame stroke, and wiper lines, while the side window gets a similar dark glass fill with stroke detailing.

Now I'm moving on to the grille, hazard light, sign, and emblem SVGs: the grille has grey horizontal slats on a dark background without the glow effect for a steel look, the hazard light is a yellow rectangle with black diagonal stripe polygons drawn programmatically in a loop, the sign has a dark background with cyan border, magenta "NOMAD-77" text, and a cyan subtitle, and the emblem is a hexagonal shape at a 100x100 viewBox.

I'm adding more textures too: vents with dark slots and amber lines, pods arranged as a 3x2 grid of ringed circles, a small rear license plate reading "2077-MIL", and a faded white "UNIT 07" stencil decal for the cab doors. That brings the total to ten textures, and I'm working out the aspect ratios for the bumper planes so the hazard texture doesn't distort too much when applied. Now I'm setting up a helper function to generate the geometry for each piece before writing the full code.

Setting up imports and helper functions...

Still writing wheel geometry...

Still positioning wheel lugs and sketching tire tread detail as a ring of small boxes around the tire's circumference.

Checking the lug clearance at the bottom of each wheel, I'm raising the wheel center to .72 so the lowest lug only sinks about 5cm, staying within 2% of truck height. Each wheel comes to 24 parts, so six wheels total 144, keeping the overall part count comfortably under 1000.

Now I'm writing the cab shape as an extruded polygon with a beveled profile, oriented so its outline maps along the vehicle's depth and height axes, giving it a paneled, slightly rounded hull look. I'm also setting up the fenders as steel boxes mounted above each wheel pair with an added flange box for the outer edge, positioning the front fender near the cab's forward z-position.

I'm placing the rear container as a camo-colored box spanning most of the vehicle's width and length behind the cab, then building the underbody frame as a dark box running the vehicle's length. I'm adding a sub-frame box to fill the gap between the frame top and container bottom, checking that its width clears the tire inner edges and that the cab sits flush on the frame. I'm deciding to skip side skirt armor and planning to write out the rest of the geometry in a reasonably sized, dense script, now positioning the windshield coordinates.

Writing windshield and decal placement...

Positioning door seams and handle geometry around the window span...

Now adding wheel steps near the tire area and sketching the side mirror arm and housing with its mounting position, then moving on to the roof.

Adding the roof lightbar with alternating colored glow segments and a base bar, plus a sensor dome and remote weapon station mounted on the roof surface.

I'm placing the RWS turret box and barrel with a cyan sensor glow, then adding a dish via lathe geometry and thin antenna rods on the cab and container roofs with glowing red tips, along with container roof plating details before starting the rear turret.

Now I'm building the turret housing with a glowing torus ring at its base, a front mantlet wedge, and the railgun's dual rail boxes running along the length of the barrel assembly.

Still writing barrel details...

The pod placement overlaps the turret ring, so I'm repositioning them forward between the cab and turret at z=-0.2, checking clearances against the rails and barrel coil, then setting the front-facing decal direction on the pods.

I'm considering whether to tilt the pods upward slightly, deciding the rotation math is getting fiddly and it's simpler to leave them straight for now. Next I'm placing ammo boxes at the rear top and working out the position and lathe axis for the radar dish near the turret housing, checking it clears the turret's rear edge.

Now I'm adding roof vents and a small antenna array, then working out the rear bumper placement relative to the chassis frame, the hazard plane at the very back, glowing red tail lights, and vertical door seam/handle bars near the rear corners.

I'm positioning a rear license plate decal on the lower rear panel, double-checking it clears the bumper and subframe geometry so it sits flush against the container's back face. Next I'll add a tow hook, underglow lighting, and spiked cone teeth along the front bumper.

Now I'm placing amber fog lights and a hazard decal on the front bumper, spacing them so they clear the spike teeth, then starting on a DRL strip glow beneath the hood.

Working out the grille decal placement by computing the slanted face's normal vector so the panel sits flush against the angled bumper surface.

Now I'm placing side decals - signs and emblems on the left and right panels at specific heights, plus working out rib positions along the body using repeated steel boxes for the horizontal rails.

Adding armor tile rows...

Adding mud flap position behind the rear wheel, then a glowing red antenna tip sphere, a feed rod connecting the dish to its focal point, and a hazard stripe pattern generator for the warning sign using alternating polygons in a monospace bold font. Now I'm finalizing the code for correct syntax before wrapping up.

Setting up the hull and camo paint presets by layering mottled color blends with panel and rivet details, then applying those paints across the extruded cab shape and container box geometry. I'm also double-checking the rod helper function signature for connecting points with a steel-colored cylinder.

The lathe outline point types should infer correctly from the inline array literal's contextual typing, so I think everything checks out and I'm ready to write the final code.
